thread:
sara_support: Hey team — acme-corp (tenant-acme-42) reporting a surge of 429s on /v1/embeddings since ~2026-03-16 23:50 UTC. Customer insists they didn't change anything, says errors started after midnight local. Can infra check quotas/burst and routing attribution?

mike_infra: Looking into it now. I can already see a sharp tokens/min spike for tenant-acme-42 starting 23:48. Possible burst window exhaustion. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/d/limits/tenant-usage?tenant=tenant-acme-42 :eyes:

anya_prodops: Can you grab a few log lines with route/model + 429 reason? We need to attribute to route vs model or global quota.

sara_support: Pasting sample from logs: `2026-03-16T23:49:58Z ERROR 429 route=embeddings model=openembed-v1 tenant=tenant-acme-42 tokens=1800 reason=burst_exhausted` — customer reports peaks ~6k tokens/min.

mike_infra: Confirmed. Quick metrics I ran: `sum(rate(tokens_total{tenant="tenant-acme-42",route="embeddings"}[1m])) by (model)` -> openembed-v1: 3.2k tpm, redwood/embeddings-quant: 2.6k tpm over 2m window. So traffic split across two model variants, but aggregate exceeded burst allowance for the routing group.

josh_engineer: FYI tenant-acme-42 is on shared pool with burst_quota=5000 tokens per 60s. If it sustains >burst_quota we start returning 429s. Need to check if this is transient or sustained (could be a retry storm).

sara_support: Customer insists they made no code changes. Any way to check if clients retried or replayed requests from their side?

mike_infra: I pulled sample request_ids: `req_3f5a`, `req_3f5b`, `req_3f5c` — payloads are nearly identical and timestamps are 1s apart. Looks like a client-side retry loop or webhook replay. I'm going to DM the customer with the request_ids.

anya_prodops: Observability checklist we should do now: 1) Create alert: `increase in 429s by tenant` (e.g., rate(429_count[5m]) by (tenant) > 10) 2) Dashboard panel: tokens/min broken down by tenant+route+model (stacked) 3) Add a deeplink from support triage to the sampled request logs and to the per-tenant usage page. I'll file the infra task.

sara_support: Customer asked for a temporary quota lift while they fix the retry. Can we approve short bump?

josh_engineer: I can approve a 1-hour temporary increase. I'll apply a delta +5000 tokens/60s for tenant-acme-42 and monitor.

quota-bot: Action: temporary_quota_adjust tenant=tenant-acme-42 delta=+5000 window=60s expires=2026-03-17T00:55:00Z :white_check_mark:

mike_infra: After the temporary bump, 429s dropped within ~90s and errors decreased to normal. Metrics link: https://console.redwood.com/d/limits/tenant-raw?tenant=tenant-acme-42&range=1h — looks like client retries flattened out.

sara_support: Great — customer confirmed fewer errors. We'll keep the bump until they confirm a fix. Also adding notes to support ticket SUP-4581.

anya_prodops: Post-incident followups: - Add a dashboard tile for `429 rate by tenant` and a dedicated heatmap for `tokens/min by route+model` - Add runbook section: "How to attribute 429s to route/model/customer" with queries used above - Add a short-term telemetry capture (sampled payloads + request headers) when a tenant hits >80% burst cap.

josh_engineer: Agree. Also suggest adding a fingerprint: `tenant|route|model|burst_window` to make attribution deterministic across dashboards and alerts.

sara_support: Closing loop with the customer now. Will update SUP-4581 with actions and the temporary quota expiry. Thanks all :handshake:
